'''Dominique O'Neal Jones''' (born October 15, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Changsha Yongsheng]] of the  [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]]. A noted scorer in college at the [[University of South Florida]], Jones had the second-highest scoring average in the [[Big East Conference]] during the 2009–10 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=BIG EAST Conference – Overall Statistics|url=http://www.bigeast.org/portals/5/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2009-2010/CONFLDRS.HTM|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130414074149/http://www.bigeast.org/portals/5/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2009-2010/CONFLDRS.HTM|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 14, 2013|access-date=12 June 2012}}</ref> Jones has had a long career in the CBA and was named the league's MVP in 2023.

== College career ==

=== Freshman ===
Jones entered USF and started every game during his first season. He scored 17.1 points per game with 4.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists.

=== Sophomore ===
In Jones's second season, the sophomore improved his scoring (18.1), rebounds (5.6) and assists (3.9) averages.

=== Junior ===
Prior to the 2009–2010 season, Jones was named to the preseason All Big East team. Over the season, he averaged 21.4 points while also grabbing 6.1 rebounds and giving 3.6 assists. He scored a season high 46 points in a 109–105 win over the [[Providence Friars]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4246/dominique-jones Dominique Jones] ESPN.com</ref> USF went 20–13 and Jones was named to the 1st team All-Big East team. He led the team with the most points in a game.

== Professional career ==

[[File:Kyrie Irving (8194734863).jpg|thumb|Jones (left) guarding [[Kyrie Irving]] in 2012]]
He was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 25th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. The Grizzlies traded his rights to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for cash considerations, reported to be around $3 million.

On November 30, 2010, the Mavericks assigned Jones to the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA D-League]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70326/20101130/mavs_send_beaubois_jones_to_d_league/ |title=Mavs Send Beaubois, Jones |access-date=2010-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101203001426/http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/70326/20101130/mavs_send_beaubois_jones_to_d_league |archive-date=2010-12-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> only to be called up early January 2011 after an injury to [[Caron Butler]]. He scored nine points in his return, in a 104–95 Dallas win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/310102005|title=Mavericks 104-95 Cavaliers (Jan 2, 2011) Box Score|website=ESPN}}</ref> A foot injury sidelined him for much of the season after averaging 2.3 points in 18 games. At the end of the season, the Mavericks would win the [[2011 NBA Finals]].<ref>Sefco, Eddie. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120720125723/http://mavsblog.dallasnews.com/2011/02/dominique-jones-to-miss-significan-time.html/|title=Mavericks' rookie Dominique Jones to miss significant time with foot injury}}</ref>

On January 15, 2012, Dallas assigned Jones to the D-League again. He would be recalled a week later.<ref>[http://www.foxsportssouthwest.com/01/23/12/Mavs-recall-Dominique-Jones-from-D-Leagu/landing_mavericks.html?blockID=651498& Mavs recall Dominique Jones from D-League]</ref> On February 19, 2012, Jones made his first career three-point field goal against the [[New York Knicks]]. On March 10, 2012, Jones recorded his first career start in an 87–111 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20120310/DALGSW/gameinfo.html Mavericks–Warriors Boxscore]</ref>

In October 2012, the Mavericks opted not to pick up the team option for the next season in Jones's rookie contract. Jones was waived on March 9, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/inside_report/practice-report-marions-status-vs-t-wolves-undetermined-mavs-cut-ties-dojo|title=Practice report: Marion's status vs. T-Wolves undetermined, Mavs cut ties with DoJo|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> On March 19, he was acquired by the [[Springfield Armor]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/springfield_acquires_former_nb_2013_03_18.html |title=Springfield Acquires Former NBA Champion Dominique Jones |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-03-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204005532/http://www.nba.com/dleague/springfield/springfield_acquires_former_nb_2013_03_18.html |archive-date=2013-12-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He joined the Milwaukee Bucks for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. In September 2013, he joined the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/09/dominique-jones-jonny-flynn-to-play-in-china.html|title=Dominique Jones, Jonny Flynn To Play In China|website=Hoops Rumors}}</ref>

On October 11, 2014, he signed with the [[Jilin Northeast Tigers]] for the [[2014–15 CBA season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/137336/jilin-northeast-tigers-signing-dominique-jones.html|title=Jilin Northeast Tigers signing Dominique Jones}}</ref> Following the CBA season, he signed with [[Atenienses de Manatí (basketball)|Atenienses de Manatí]] on March 18 for the rest of the 2015 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/155716/dominique-jones-replaces-cummings-in-atenienses-de-manati.html|title=Dominique Jones replaces Cummings in Atenienses de Manatì}}</ref>

On July 8, 2015, Jones returned to China and signed with [[Shanxi Zhongyu]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/167696/shanxi-zhongyu-sign-dominique-jones.html|title=Shanxi Zhongyu sign Dominique Jones}}</ref> In December 2015, he parted ways with Shanxi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/185762/akognon-dalembert-franklin-and-jordan-signed-in-cba-in-december.html|title=Akognon, Dalembert, Franklin and Jordan signed in CBA in December}}</ref>

On August 23, 2016, Jones signed with [[Qingdao DoubleStar]] for the [[2016–17 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Qingdao Eagles land Dominique Jones|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/460058/Qingdao-Eagles-land-Dominique-Jones|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=August 23, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref>

On August 11, 2017, Jones signed with [[Nanjing Monkey Kings]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/jj-hickson-and-dominique-jones-sign-with-jiangsu-tongxi-106043434/|title=J.J. Hickson and Dominique Jones sign with Jiangsu Tongxi|website=247Sports}}</ref> On December 12, 2017, he was waived by the Nanjing Monkey Kings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/cba/2017-12-12/doc-ifypnyqi4301233.shtml|title=同曦官方宣布更换外援 前CBA助攻王加盟|date=December 12, 2017|website=sports.sina.com.cn}}</ref>

On January 11, 2018, Jones signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/asia/iran/260800/dominique-jones-signs-with-petrochimi.html Dominique Jones signs with Petrochimi]{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On August 7, 2018, Jones signed with the [[Jilin Northeast Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=Jones comes back to Jilin Tigers |url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/543177/Jones-comes-back-to-Jilin-Tigers |publisher=Asia-Basket |access-date=August 7, 2018 |date=August 7, 2018}}</ref> In the 2022–23 season, Jones led the league in assists and steals and was named the league's International MVP.

On August 25, 2023, Jones moved to the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dominique Jones moves to Xinjiang for new CBA season-Xinhua |url=https://english.news.cn/20230825/aedd9411051241339afcc26c59580a7d/c.html |access-date=2024-04-01 |website=english.news.cn}}</ref>

On September 25, 2024, Jones signed with the Jilin Northeast Tigers.<ref>{{cite web |title=正式官宣！东北虎功勋外援琼斯新赛季正式回归 |url=https://news.cnjiwang.com/jwyc/202409/3886259.html |publisher=中国吉林网 |access-date=25 September 2024 |date=25 September 2024}}</ref>

=== The Basketball Tournament ===
In 2017, Jones competed in [[The Basketball Tournament]] with the Tampa Bulls, a team made up of USF alumni. Jones' team made it to the Sweet 16 where they were eliminated by eventual champions [[Overseas Elite]]. Jones led the team with 28.3 PPG during the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/players/dominique-jones |title=Dominique Jones | the Basketball Tournament |access-date=2018-03-13 |archive-date=2018-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313093403/https://www.thetournament.com/players/dominique-jones |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Jones' forearms are tattooed with the words "Hustler" and "Survivor".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-mavericks/headlines/20120712-photos-what-mavs-fans-can-expect-from-new-look-roster.ece|title=Photos: What Mavs fans can expect from new-look roster}}</ref> After the Mavericks won the [[2011 NBA Finals]], Jones then proceeded to get a tattoo on his neck of the [[Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy]], commemorating his team's victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-mavericks/headlines/20110620-dominique-jones-tattoos-nba-trophy-on-his-neck.ece|title=Dominique Jones tattoos NBA trophy on his neck}}</ref>
